rows.lesions_enrolled: not reported (plan: 5 marked lesions per leg [about 30 per arm across 6 patients, inferred])
rows.analysis_unit: not stated: groups described as lesions, number analysed given as 6 participants

rows.citation: Excimer Light Treatment for Idiopathic Guttate Hypomelanosis: A Pilot Study. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01956435; sponsor Seton Healthcare Family; results first posted 2017-10-18
rows.intervention: Xtrac excimer laser 308 nm, twice weekly for 12 weeks, standard vitiligo protocol
rows.comparator: untreated marked lesions on the opposite leg
rows.time_from_last_treatment: NOT_DERIVABLE: outcome time frame is 12 weeks from start; final photographs at a 25th visit without treatment, interval after the last treatment not stated
rows.dark_overshoot: not reported (0 of 6 other adverse events at frequency threshold 0; hyperpigmentation not named)
rows.texture_or_scar: not reported (0 of 6 other adverse events at frequency threshold 0; scarring or texture not named)
rows.source_location: Results, Outcome measure 1 (PRIMARY) Efficacy Outcome, group OG000
rows.endpoint_definition: blinded-observer grade of improvement from baseline, scale -1 to 3 (3 = full re-pigmentation on >75% IGH), reported as mean
rows.assessment_method: photographic comparison graded by masked outcome assessor ('blinded observer'; description plans two blinded dermatologists)
rows.patient_noticeability: self-reported mean 4.5 (SD 0.223) on a stated 1-to-4 scale, treated lesions (row 2)
rows.complete_match: not reported (top grade is full re-pigmentation on >75% IGH; no count of complete matches)
rows.uncertainty: Mean grade 2.31 lies between 'moderate' (2) and 'full re-pigmentation on >75%' (3); a mean grade does not say how many lesions reached any category. Adverse events: frequency threshold 0 and 0 of 6 other events, although the protocol mentions adjusting fluence 'if burning occurred'. Registry oddities across the record: (a) enrollment 6 actual vs 10 planned; (b) the detailed description plans a 1-to-5 scale rated by two blinded dermatologists, but results use a -1-to-3 scale and 'the blinded observer', so the scale changed after registration; (c) planned outcomes at weeks 4, 8 and 12 and stratification by Fitzpatrick type, but only a 12-week mean is posted and no Fitzpatrick types are given; (d) the description says control versus treatment will be statistically compared, yet no p-value or between-group test is posted; (e) result groups are described as lesions but counts are given as 6 participants, so it is not stated whether means are over lesions or patients, and within-patient clustering is not addressed [the narrow 95% CI suggests lesion-level analysis; inferred]; (f) the registry codes the design SINGLE_GROUP and 'Healthy volunteers: True' although participants have IGH and sides were randomized; (g) all 6 participants female (5 White, 1 Black or African American) with minimal variation in Fitzpatrick skin type; (h) collaborator Photomedex [from outside knowledge the maker of the Xtrac device; not stated in source] is a possible conflict of interest; (i) no follow-up after treatment ('lack of extended follow-up'), so nothing here tests a match lasting six months; (j) same cohort as the journal article filed as gordon2017: do not count as a separate study when pooling.
